clauses.text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER
Amendment  of Executive  O rder N o. 8257  
of S eptember 21, 1939, A uthorizing  
Excepted A ppointments  T o M eet 
Public E xigency
Executive Order No. 8257 2  of Sep­
tember 21, 1939, authorizing excepted  
appointments to meet public exigency,  
is hereby amended to read as follows:
“By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by paragraph Eighth, subdivision  
SECOND, section 2 of the Civil Service  
Act (22 Stat. 404), it is hereby ordered  
as follows:
“Whenever, because of a public exi­
gency directly connected with the na-
15 CFR Part 50.  
*4 F U . 4023.
tional-defense program, or because of  
the urgency for the immediate filling of  
a position involved in such program, the  
Civil Service Commission determines  
that it is in the public interest to do so,  
it may authorize the filling of any posi­
tion connected with the national-defense  
program for a term not extending beyond  
the duration of the national-defense  
program, without regard to the competi­
tive requirements of the Civil Service  
Rules, subject to such noncompetitive  
tests of fitness as the Commission may  
prescribe. Persons so appointed will not  
thereby acquire a classified (competi­
tive) civil service status.”

ACT:EO:8564>EO:9830.effective_basis: Express wording in the enacting clause: "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:" (span in effective_wording), which introduces Parts I, II and III alike; Part III (the revocation list) has no separate date. Signed "February 24, 1947" (signature block after the last Part III row); FR filed Feb. 24, 1947, published 12 FR 1259 of 1947-02-25. The OFR disposition note date 1947-02-24 is the signing date, not the effective date. Reading that the preamble date governs Part III is the natural one but the reviewer must accept or reject it.

ACT:EO:8564>EO:9830.notes: EO 9830 Part III (OCR heading "P art  H I") is a single sentence "The following Executive orders are hereby revoked:" followed by a one-per-line list of 54 orders (52 numbered, 2 unnumbered; EO 8894 and EO 9004 are among them), ending at the signature block; no savings, exception or 'nothing herein' wording found anywhere in the held text (searched nothing in/herein, shall not affect, heretofore, remain/continue in effect, saving, notwithstanding). The FR contents table on PDF page 2 also lists these numbers ("Executive orders revoked" finding aid); the naming span is taken from Part III itself, not the finding aid. Target row 'No. 8564 of October 8, 1940.': number and date match the target's signing date (1940-10-08). DOSSIER DEFECT: the clause inventory for EO:8564 (offsets 736-1250) is EO 8563 (Schedule A Subdivision VII para. 5, temporary postal holiday workers), footer '[No. 8563]' (OCR 'tNo. 8563]'); EO 8564's own text is the following 'Amendment of Executive Order No. 8257' ending at the '[No. 8564]' footer. An inventory override is needed before any claim. AI producer hypothesis; not a review, status or certification. Agent-located record (act_overrides); an independent AI review upheld it. Hypothesis only: not human certification and not a status.
ACT:EO:8564>EO:9830.producer_d6: Searched held FR texts 1940-1947 for EO 8564 and EO 8257: no instrument other than EO 9830 names either after 1940-10-08. EO 8564's operative act is a whole-text amendment of EO 8257; its substituted text has a term on appointments ('for a term not extending beyond the duration of the national-defense program'), which limits appointments, not the order. LEAD (scope, not an end): EO 9063 (1942-02-16) War Service Regulations created a separate war-service appointment route; they do not name EO 8564/8257. Dossier chain empty; no own-term end. No earlier end found in held sources. EO 9830 revokes both EO 8257 and EO 8564 by separate rows.

"8564" hits after 1940: EO 8833/8834 (1941-07, see below); others are F.R. Doc./page numbers (EO 8940, 9586/9587, 9728). Read held EO_8564.txt own text (whole-text amendment of EO 8257; appointments "for a term not extending beyond the duration of the national-defense program", a term on appointments, not on the order).
